approver: Tauquir Ahmed (owner), who on 2026-11-10 chose the rule that an unknown publish outcome keeps the caller's slot, including this prior-test edit, after the #1732 review
scope: One prior test and nothing else. test_queue_admission.py: test_a_schedule_cancelled_mid_publish_releases_its_reservation becomes test_a_schedule_cancelled_mid_publish_keeps_its_slot_for_the_retry: the same cancel mid-publish, now asserting, through the caller's cap count (`_cap_count`), that the caller still holds one slot and that, once its retry of the same topic lands, it holds one slot still (counted once); the docstring says why. No other test, helper or fixture changes.
reason: OME-1859 (spec docs/spec/2026-11-10-jetstream-publish-unknown-outcome.md, D1-D3): a JetStream publish is at-least-once, so after the run's own send goes unanswered, or a cancel lands while it is in flight, the broker may have stored the run. Releasing the slot there let a stored run execute uncounted (the #1648 review's two repros). This test pinned the release on a cancel mid-publish; it now pins the held slot and that the landed retry is counted once.
